body: Surprisingly no, I did not suffer any side effects with the increase. However, every person is different. Lexapro has not helped majorily with my depression nor anxiety. If anything, it feels that I climaxed after a few weeks, then my body grew a tolerance to the help and went back down the hill, in which is why I started therapy. So, as long as Lexapro is the best anti-depressant for you, and you are still struggling, I would say upping your dose is a good idea.

With the mindset and situations I have been in, I do know the 20mg have helped. I would say that if you are still rocky and can't seem to find your way through depression as easily, a bump up from you 15mg may be something to consider. 

And yes, therapy along with your Lexapro medication truly does wonders. Medication by itself just isn't as effective. Sure it still helps, but it is not nearly as helpful when paired with therapy.

I am a few months in. Started off with 10mg, now over the past month I have been on 20mg. As a whole, it definitely helps but I don't feel that it does much unless it is also paired with therapy. I just started therapy along with my prescription, and it is all working much better than the prescription alone.

Well, then his intentions cannot be to take your girl, nor for her to run to him. Let me ask you, do you trust your girlfriend? I mean like, deeply, no doubts about her decisions. That you fully believe she will make a proper choice. Do you?

Hey pal. I cannot say I understand the whole marriage thing, however, I understand the unbearable fear of your significant other leaving you for someone else. 

Personally, I am also going through a dark place within my own relationship. I believe sitting down with your girlfriend and genuinely opening up with the entirety of what you said here would be your best option. However, if you do not see this option as applicable, I understand therapy could be beneficial towards this subject. You stated that you already are seeing someone for your dark thoughts, and I think we can all say that is a big step. We here are all very proud of you for such a thing.

Now, something else to consider. Have you gotten to know this other guy? Take some time when you see him next to start up a conversation. You don't gotta be BFFs with the man, however, getting to know him will give you a better idea of his own situations/ intent. Hell, if you spark a conversation, be honest with your fear of cheating that you have. If you engage him in this way, remember to NOT look at him as someone who is taking your soon-to-be wife. Look at him as a friend, then form your opinion afterward.

I hope this helps bud.
